items.title: EchoFG: display timing (the generated frame's present blocks 17-20 ms): vsync / VRR / frame latency
items.note: 2026-10-11 retest (x3 at about 30 fps, 4K 120 Hz, GPU scaling on): the FSR path's generated-frame Present takes 16.7-18.4 ms, EchoFG's 6.4-6.9 ms: the long wait was FSR's. With EchoFG the display shows two presents inside one refresh in about 19% of cases (refresh gaps 0:157 1:460 2:200; FSR path 0:~2) and the presenting thread comes back only 1.6 ms before the next real frame (FSR path 6-7 ms): 90 presents a second on a 120 Hz screen with little slack. Open: is VRR really on (Sync mode Default = interval 0, no tearing flag?), and the slack. Owner, 2026-10-11: Lossless Scaling's Sync mode changed to Off (allow tearing): nothing visible changes; Sync mode stays as it was. (The log had no new session after it yet, so the refresh-gap line for that setting is not measured.) BUILT 2026-10-11 (deployed to D: next): presents are put one to a refresh of the display (setting 'Put the presents one to a refresh of the display', on by default; from DXGI frame statistics; switches itself off on a variable refresh). The log says 'the presents are put one to a refresh ... (a steady N Hz refresh)' or why not. Offline it can only show 'not steady' (this machine's G-Sync window), so whether it is active at the owner's, and whether the 0-gaps (19%) go away, is for the live log: `dev.py logs` prints the per-engine gap shares. Audit of the presenter after that (2026-10-11): (1) the display statistics were never reset for a new swap chain, so a counter that restarted read as '4294967278 presents not seen' in the log (fixed: they start again with each swap chain, device or backwards count); (2) the refresh alignment's slot memory could drift into the future after a restart and pile all the presents at the end of the interval (fixed: forgotten after 100 ms, and it steps aside when the presents of one real frame cannot fit the refreshes, e.g. x7 at 30 fps on 120 Hz); (3) its 'steady' test took ~13 stretches to settle (fixed: 2).

items.title: The recorder is ONE feature of the manager (Features tab, Recording), no longer a section in each addon
items.where: manager/src/features/recorder_{service,feature}.*; IHost API 1.3; addons: runtime.cpp Record() shim, echofg_addon.cpp; tools/recorder_test.cpp
items.note: DONE 2026-10-19 (built, offline-tested; NOT yet seen live in Lossless Scaling). The manager owns the recorder: settings (config.json section 'Recorder'), the hotkey (Ctrl+Shift+F1..F12, polled on its own thread), saving, memory, folder, a beep and a note (<file>.lsrec.json) beside each file, 'Keep going after the key', a ten-second clip with the rolling buffer off. It finds LSFG's captured frames itself (a FrameTap per context, hooked at the manager's own dispatch hook: D3D11Hook::SetDispatchObserver), so no addon has to be on. Addons (NR, the upscalers, EchoFG) only offer what the manager cannot see (presented frames before their picture, NIS's input, EchoFG's frames) through IHost::RecorderOffer; compare mode saves each mode with RecorderSave; the event EAM_EVENT_RECORDING_SAVED makes them write their frame trace beside a file. Addon API 1.3 (the addons' min_host_version is 1.3.0). Removed from the addons: the Recorder instance, the Recording settings and panel section, the shared-setting mirroring, TapForRecording (the interim fix of the same day). Tests: eam_recordertest (manager), the host test runs the real service (record_replay, record_addon_off), settings tests. items.title: DLSS-G feasibility probe (Streamline sl_dlss_g, own motion, flat depth): works, but EchoFG and FSR are better on the same footage
items.where: docs/mfg-super-motion-study.md; tools (new nr_dlssg_probe); external/ngx headers (public NVIDIA SDK)
items.note: 2026-10-20: MFG Super Motion 1.0.2 (files in NEW FILES/research, not in git) shows the method: NGX D3D12 DLSS-G with estimated motion (NVIDIA optical flow or own pyramid flow with a forward-backward check) and a constant depth plane; still-pixel passes keep the HUD. Ours: a probe tool, this card (Ada, x2), every return code reported; then the same with EchoFG's flow. Rules: no driver-profile edits, no architecture spoofing, no third-party kernel packages, nothing of theirs copied. 2026-10-20 RESULT: tools/dlssg_probe (Streamline 2.14.16 in external/, not in git) initialises DLSS-G from a non-game with engine type + own project GUID (no NVIDIA application id: refused with id 0), status ok, 2 frames shown per real frame (x2 on Ada), flat depth and our own motion accepted. NOT yet known: picture quality (screen grab is not a reliable tap); look by eye: onlygen=1 mvec=exact vs wrong. Product shape: DLSS-G owns the swap chain, so it can only be the final presenter of an own window (like EchoFG nr_fgpresent), not inside LS. Licence/application-id question for a release is open. EYE TEST 2026-10-20 (owner): three windows (exact, wrong, wrong again; the 2nd and 3rd overlapped by mistake): all jumped at the start (the first second, DLSS-G warming up: frame timer reset); exact and the 3rd looked more shimmery than the 2nd, so NO clear difference between exact and wrong motion: inconclusive, and it may mean DLSS-G does not rely on the vectors we give it (it has its own optical flow). Next: one run at a time, a numeric test (needs the generated frame read back), then EchoFG flow in place of the constant. MEASURED 2026-10-20 (Desktop Duplication + check_grab.py, 1 - correlation): generated frames half way between real ones; exact vectors + FLAT depth = as clean as real frames (0.0043 vs 0.0043, 8 and 40 px/frame); zero vectors 0.0046 (8 px) / 0.0159 (40 px); wrong 0.0159 / 0.0334 (worst 0.127). DLSS-G uses our motion and its quality follows it: our flow field is the lever. Next probe: several motions + a static HUD patch, then EchoFG flow from a recorded clip. HARDER PROBE 2026-10-20 (real footage, EchoFG flow estimator as the vectors, truth = the odd clip frames): DLSS-G+flow beats the plain blend of the two real frames by +0.068 / +0.016 / +0.003 (1-corr scale, three clips), flow beats zero motion by 0.05-0.08 on moving footage; so a modest gain, not a jump. Open: score EchoFG own synthesis and FSR on the same truth with the same scorer. HEAD TO HEAD 2026-10-20 (same scorer, gain over the blend, three clips): DLSS-G+our flow +0.068/+0.016/+0.003; FSR 3.1 +0.090/+0.098/+0.037; EchoFG synthesis +0.096/+0.111/+0.039. No case for a DLSS-G generator in the products; keep the motion-side ideas (persistent HUD mask, input lag, flow consistency check) as new cards. Related: I9, E1, E2, E3.

items.title: EchoFG flow: a forward-backward consistency check and a median over the neighbours' motion (compare with FlowEstimator's present median)
items.note: Their pyramid flow keeps a vector only if its way back comes home within about a texel and a half, else takes the best neighbouring one that does. Ours has a 3x3 vector median and a distrust mask; measure whether a back-check adds anything (E8 gap to the oracle). RESULT 2026-10-20 (lab, tools/flowlab/check_lab.py): the way-back check replaces 11-15 % of pixels and gains +0.06..+0.14 dB on a one-field draw, +0.01..+0.08 on the direct draw; the way back made by splatting the forward field alone gives nearly all of it. Marginal for a pass of about a ms: NOT built into the estimator. See docs/mfg-super-motion-engine-notes.md.

items.title: NVIDIA optical flow hardware (NVOFA) against our flow estimator on the recordings
items.note: DONE 2026-10-20. Our estimator beats NVOFA on all four clips (by 0.4-1.3 dB at NVOFA's best setting; photometric error 4-5x lower); a per-pixel fusion of the two equals ours; NVOFA needs the picture at 1/2 size or smaller for the large motions here (limited reach) and a GRAYSCALE8 input (ABGR8 gave nonsense). Cost 0.4 ms a 720p pair on its own engine. No quality case; a speed idea only (E14).

items.title: Seed our flow search from NVOFA's vectors (or replace the coarse levels) to cut the estimator's GPU time on a full card
items.note: A speed idea for the GPU-limit use case, NVIDIA cards only, a driver dependency (nvofapi64.dll). Measure first how much of the estimator's time the coarse levels take (FlowEstimator::TakeStageTimes; the lab does not read it yet); only worth it if that is most of it. Number to beat (2026-10-20): the estimate costs 4-5.5 ms a pair at 2560x1440 on the 4070 Ti SUPER (search about half).

items.title: EchoFG flow: a far search for thin fast things (second largest level, accepted only where it fits clearly better)
items.note: A lamp post past a wall, a thin limb. Test clip needed (record one); score with tools/flowlab. RESULT 2026-10-20 (lab): no gain: the estimator already tracks the 31 px/frame pole of the made-up scene; the idea changed 0.1 % of the pixels. Closed.

items.title: EchoFG flow: the picture at large per tile as the fallback for plain blocks and repeating textures
items.where: docs/mfg-super-motion-engine-notes.md step 8; E2 (blocky cells on periodic textures)
items.note: 4K 2026-10-20: EchoFG took a 4K game from ~50 to ~14 fps; the motion is now estimated at half size from 2561 px wide (NR_ANALYSIS_SCALE), live log confirms it ran (real frames 11-17 ms apart, EchoFG GPU 3.4-4.1 ms); user confirmed it looked good. GPU 2026-10-20: built as nr::FlowFix (flow_fix.cpp), in EchoFG test build (NR_FLOW_FIX=0 off): made-up scene +9.94 -> +12.59 dB, real clips unchanged (+0.00..+0.02), 3.8 ms/pair at 2560x1440. Waiting for a real fence/tower-face clip. The dominant motion of found, textured blocks per tile (weighted toward those near it); a block that shows little, or repeats, takes it when the two real frames agree under it about as well as under its own. LAB 2026-10-20 (tools/flowlab/field_lab.py, make_synth_clip.py): fixes the repeating-block failure (+4.0 dB in that region, error 182 -> 10; the estimator reads it as no motion) but the simple rule changes 50-65 % of real pixels (-0.07..+0.10 dB) and hurts a pole and a plain block. Needs a robust per-tile vector (a mode), a real repeating test and the way-back check; and a real clip with a fence / tower face / railing to settle it. Open.

items.title: EchoFG: smooth the motion field (outlier replacement, then a similarity-weighted 5x5 mean) before drawing
items.note: Seven of eight neighbours agree and the place is further away: take theirs; then the mean of the 25 words weighted by nearness of each word to its own and by whether both frames show it. RESULT 2026-10-20 (lab): +0.00..+0.05 dB on real clips: no gain (the estimator's own median and pixel pass already smooth). Closed.

items.title: EchoFG synthesis: try the direct draw (motion at the pixel being made from both fields, nothing carried) in place of splat + hypotheses + holes
items.note: MEASURED 2026-10-20 on 12 pairs of three clips: direct from two real flow fields = EchoFG's synthesis within 0.1 dB (+2.12/+2.22/+1.92 vs +2.09/+2.23/+2.00 dB over the blend), with no splat buffers or atomics: a possible cost saving at equal quality. Needs the second flow (A to C) or the way-back check. Next: all clips with nr_fgeval, then GPU cost, then live. RESULT 2026-10-20: built into own_synth (owndirect=1, a second estimate the other way round): quality equal to the splat synthesis over six clips (mean -0.01 dB), but the second estimate costs about the estimate again (4-5.5 ms at 1440p) and the direct pass was not cheaper than Synth: NOT adopted, kept as an experiment. The estimate itself (4-5 ms, half of it the search) is the big cost: E14 now has a number to beat; a way-back check from the first estimate's own vectors (E12) is the cheap route to a second field.
